items.title: Nurse booked after newborn’s thumb accidentally severed at Pindi's Holy Family Hospital
items.description: RAWALPINDI: A nurse was booked by police for mistakenly chopping off the thumb of a newborn baby girl in the nursery ward of Rawalpindi Holy Family Hospital. Police investigating the incident said efforts were underway to trace and investigate the accused nurse, who had not been available so far. They said the exact circumstances in which the child’s thumb was cut off would be known after the investigation. Qasir Mehmood, the father of the child and a resident of Hassan Abdal, lodged an FIR with New Town police, stating that his 23-day-old daughter had been admitted to the Holy Family Hospital’s nursery ward for treatment after being born at the hospital. He said that when he visited his daughter on Thursday evening, he found that her right thumb had been cut off. After he inquired from the doctor, he was told that a nurse had mistakenly cut off the child’s thumb during treatment in the nursery ward. The doctor informed him that the hospital would conduct an inquiry and let him know what had happened, he stated in the FIR. After the complaint was lodged, local police reached the hospital and later registered a case under the relevant section of the law. Meanwhile, the father of the newborn told Dawn on Friday that the nurse had joined the hospital’s inquiry and revealed the circumstances in which the child’s thumb was cut off. “I have forgiven her after she apologised,” he said. Separately, a Bykea rider was deprived of his motorcycle, cash and cell phone by three unidentified persons after reaching their destination in Ratta Amral. Usman Ali complained to the police that while carrying three passengers on his motorcycle near Mandi Mor, he was taken to a deserted place where one of the passengers held him at gunpoint and snatched his motorcycle, cell phone and Rs800. Police have registered a case and initiated an investigation into the incident. Published in Dawn, July 25th, 2026

items.title: Folly of chasing exchange rate
items.description: PAKISTAN’S economic debate is trapped in outdated vocabulary. Each time the rupee weakens, headlines scream ‘devaluation’. Anchors ask whether one is imminent, while policymakers debate whether the exchange rate should be defended or strengthened. as if it was simply another policy tool. It’s not. The language belongs to another era. Today, most countries let their currencies move more freely. When an economy gets dangerously out of balance, the currency has to adjust to avoid a more disruptive crisis, as our own history has shown. The exchange rate is not an administrative decision. It is the market price of one country’s currency in terms of another. This price is shaped by domestic inflation relative to that of the country’ trading partners and the accompanying interest-rate differentials, productivity, government spending more than it earns, external balances, capital flows, adequacy of foreign currency reserves and, above all, expectations of what businesses think will happen to the economy in the future. The rupee doesn’t get weaker because policymakers decide to weaken it. It weakens because the country’s economic choices make the current rate impossible to maintain. Central banks try to manage this by choosing different systems — a fixed rate, a managed float of the currency or a freely floating rate. Each regime imposes its own discipline but no system allows a government to control the exchange rate without fixing the bigger economic picture first. Pakistan has drifted between these arrangements without consistently committing to any of them — tightly managed at times, allowed to depreciate gra­­dually at others, restrained through administrative controls, or adjusted only under IMF-sup­ported programmes. This is not a coherent strategy; it’s a succession of ad hoc responses to recurring crises. People often think a weaker rupee is the main reason Pakistan struggles to export. The real determinants of competitiveness lie elsewhere. Exporters here face far greater structural obstacles than the exchange rate itself: expensive and unreliable electricity and energy, high taxes and unpredictable cumbersome regulations, outdated shipping logistics and inefficient customs procedures. Furthermore, a modest depreciation cannot compensate for structural impediments of this scale when high tariffs, non-tariff barriers and regulatory restrictions distort relative prices far more than movements in the exchange rate. While domestic producers remain insulated from global competition whether the rupee appreciates or depreciates, exporters face elevated costs for imported inputs. The exchange rate is just a symptom of how the economy is being run. The exchange rate is just a symptom of how the economy is being run. Exchange-rate stability depends on policy credibility rather than administrative intervention. It requires fiscal discipline, low and predictable inflation, sustainable external balances, competitive domestic markets and confidence that macroeconomic policies are internally consistent. Persistent fiscal deficits financed through borrowing fuel inflation, erode confidence and render the exchange rate unsustainable; propping up an artificially strong currency merely postpones adjustment while increasing its eventual cost. Economists often refer to the fancy term ‘REER’ (real effective exchange rate). This is a diagnostic tool which simply compares Pakistan’s prices with the prices of its trading partners, accounting for inflation, to see if the rupee looks broadly overpriced or underpriced. It does not magically tell you the ‘perfect’ price of the rupee, especially when the government is heavily interfering with trade and import rules. Its utility also depends on the structure of the economy: where trade is open and prices respond freely to market forces, REER is informative; where protection, import restrictions and administrative controls are extensive, its relevance diminishes, since tariffs, licensing requirements, customs delays and regulatory barriers shape competition more than the exchange rate does. Governments can temporarily influence the measured REER through tariffs, exchange controls, multiple exchange rates or import restrictions. These may ease immediate pressure on currency, but do not improve competitiveness. Instead, they create shortages and widen the gap between official and market exchange rates. The official exchange rate may appear stable even while the underlying equilibrium is drifting away. The State Bank can and should intervene to reduce excessive short-term volatility and maintain orderly market conditions. What it cannot do is permanently offset weak fiscal, monetary and structural policies. Markets eventually prevail. Pakistan’s experience illustrates this. The country has repeatedly moved through the same cycle: an overvalued exchange rate, declining reserves, import restrictions, IMF support, sharp depreciation and temporary stability before the next crisis emerged. Adjustment then came through panic and sharp devaluation. Each episode was descri­bed as a currency crisis, whereas a market-responsive rate would have allowed gradual correction and reduced crises. The exchange rate merely exposed underlying weaknesses and the failure to undertake timely fiscal and structural reforms. To be fair, today’s circumstances differ from previous crises. They look admittedly better: the current account is broadly balanced, reserves have stabilised, the gap between official and unofficial exchange rates has largely disappeared, and importers and exporters can obtain foreign exchange without significant rationing. But this stability should not be mistaken for a durable improvement in fundamentals. It has been supported by exceptionally strong remittance inflows, continued external borrowings, and foreign debt rollovers, subdued import demand owing to weak economic activity, high inflation that has compressed domestic demand, and the State Bank directing money changers to surrender remittances into the formal banking systems, factors that ease pressure on the rupee without removing Pakistan’s structural vulnerabilities. More importantly, per capita incomes are not growing and the investment/GDP ratio remains very low. For lasting exchange-rate stability, the priorities are clear: restore fiscal discipline, reduce inflation, reform SOEs, lower trade protection, rationalise energy pricing, improve productivity, modernise logistics and create a more predictable regulatory environment. These reforms, and not attempts to manage the exchange rate, will determine the rupee’s stability. The exchange rate is not the disease. It is merely the thermometer. Breaking the thermometer does not cure the fever. Nor does fixing the reading change the patient’s condition. The rupee simply reflects the economy Pakistan has built. Until the economy becomes more competitive and fiscally disciplined, markets will determine where the exchange rate settles. Nadeem ul Haque is former VC PIDE and deputy chair of the Planning Commission. Shahid Kardar is a former governor of the State Bank of Pakistan. Published in Dawn, July 25th, 2026

items.title: Healing touch needed
items.description: SINCE early this month, Balochistan has been reeling from a series of dastardly terror attacks. The nexus of ideologically different banned terrorist groups — the religiously motivated extremists of the TTP and BLA terrorists — poses a grave challenge. The current spate of violence started on July 5, when terrorists managed to reach the fertile Shaban area next to Hanna-Urak in the suburbs of Quetta cantonment, and then launched another attack the next day on the Mangi Dam Ziarat police post at the pumping station. Despite a valiant fight put up by a DSP and 40 policemen, the terrorists, who had attacked in a large numbers, kidnapped and killed 27 ammunition-deficient law-enforcement personnel. Timely reinforcements by the police and FC could have prevented this tragedy. Meanwhile, an FC convoy was attacked near Khad Kucha, district Mastung, resulting in casualties. In addition, a military contingent in unmarked vehicles was attacked at Bela-Vinder by the BLA’s Majeed Brigade, resulting in casualties in double figures. Clashes in the mineral-rich district of Chagai were also reported, while a suicide attack took place in Khuzdar in which a tribal political leader involved in internecine strife lost 17 of his kinsmen to five attackers who rammed their explosive-laden vehicle into the gate of the fortified compound in Wadh. A three-hour gun battle left 30 injured. In the latest high-profile incident on Thursday, a sessions judge and his guard were killed on the road by assailants. Since July 5, there have been more than 40 police, military, FC and civilian casualties, while a total of 121 terrorists have been eliminated. The operation is to continue “until the last terrorist is neutralised” say the state authorities. The government has agreed to constitute a judicial commission to probe the Urak violence and Mangi Dam tragedy. Hopefully, a judge of the high court will probe what led to the violence, in which there were four casualties among the local land owners in the agriculturally rich Shaban area around Killi Babri. The question is, how did the armed terrorist groups get involved? Similarly, Mangi is a project of national interest. It will supply fresh water to Quetta and its cantonment and reduce water shortage by around 20 per cent when operational. FC is deployed at the main dam and other ancillary sites. How come the pumping station post which was recently taken over from the defunct levies, was not being jointly manned by the FC and police, especially in light of the threat alerts issued? The most significant concern is the large number of TTP terrorists who have become active in the vast terrain joining Quetta’s suburbs to the mountainous region linking the northern parts of Balochistan with KP. During the 1980s, under martial law, Gen Ziaul Haq focused on reconciliation and good governance. The best police and civil administration officers were posted to focus on the administration of justice and service delivery. On promotion as SP and on top of my batch, I was allocated to Balochistan where for the next four years I served as additional SP Quetta, district SP Sibi in charge of the Kachi and Sibi districts and Dera Bugti and Kohlu agencies, and finally as SSP Quetta. We respected the citizens who reciprocated the sentiment. The military, police and civil administration worked for the welfare and progress of the province. Roads were safe for travel. Next, I had the honour of serving as IG Balochistan in 2007 under Gen Musharraf’s military hybrid rule. The entire province was converted into a police jurisdiction replacing the ragtag levies model of rural policing. The issue of missing persons and enforced disappearances became a festering wound in the Baloch psyche. The killing of Nawab Bugti in a cave near Kohlu sparked intense violence. The experienced Balochistan police chief needs full government support. After the 2008 elections, the PPP-led federal and provincial governments were unable to stop the kill-and-dump strategy. Mass graves were discovered. Human rights violations multiplied. The conversion to police jurisdiction was reversed. Following the 2013 polls, the PML-N-led government adopted a carrot-and-stick approach to the violence. The first-ever non-sardar chief minister genuinely worked for political reconciliation and met the BLA and BRA leaders in London and Geneva. His efforts were scuttled in 2015. The PTI-led government in 2018 could not change the tough security stance vis-à-vis Balochistan. Since the controversial 2024 elections , the PML-N-led federal and PPP-led provincial governments have actively supported this hard security-stance, with male and female Baloch activists convicted under draconian laws. The roads are unsafe. Trade and business are in decline. Fear rules and violence is widespread. Miscreants are active in the following districts: Turbat, Kalat, Khuzdar, Nushki, Surab, Gwadar, Mastung, Panjgur, Awaran, Kachi/Bolan, Kharan, Chaghi, Kohlu, and Washuk. That’s a huge swathe of land. Police have been facing a massive challenge since the recent conversion of the entire province to police jurisdiction. The experienced CT-related, KP battle-hardened police chief of Balochistan needs full support from the federal and provincial governments in terms of human resources, infrastructure and equipment. The Zia-era model of good governance is worth consideration: give him the best officers in the ranks of SP and SSP to serve for a fixed tenure of three years. The prime minister must review his decision to depute about 20 serving military officers as district SPs in the insurgency-infested areas. This militarisation of police will be a fiasco. Balochistan suffers from many missed opportunities and unfulfilled promises. Addressing the crisis effectively requires a two-pronged strategy: decisively eliminating the terrorist threat while proactively addressing the grievances of the local population. As this paper rightly observed, “The long-term solution to Balochistan’s problem remains the political path.” The need for a serious political strategy cannot be ignored anymore. A viable dialogue and political process involving Baloch sub-nationalists and other key political and security stakeholders must be held. The state must also address the province’s socioeconomic problems fairly and urgently, as an entrenched feeling of alienation is driving the youth towards the terrorists. No matter how many we arrest or kill, their numbers are increasing exponentially. The only solution lies in good governance and political dialogue. Let the healing process begin with a reconciliation commission. The writer is a former IG of Balochistan Police. Published in Dawn, July 25th, 2026

items.title: Rampant lawlessness
items.description: THE brutal slaying of a judge and his guard in Mastung is the latest in a series of blood-drenched events that have rocked Balochistan since the start of this month. Both state functionaries and ordinary citizens have been killed in these acts of terrorism. Judge Abdul Hakeem Kakar was travelling from Quetta to Mastung with another judge and security personnel when their vehicle came under attack. The judge and his guard Muhammad Zaman did not survive. Some unverified reports indicate the IS-K claimed responsibility for the assault. IS-K has been active in the province for some years, and if its role is confirmed, it would mean it is expanding its targets. Before the judge’s martyrdom there was the Mangi Dam attack , claimed by the banned TTP, as well as a deadly assault on a Karachi-bound bus in the Khud Kocha area, and the killing of workers originally hailing from Punjab in Mashkhel. The recent wave of violence indicates the complexity of the threat in Balochistan, where terrorists belonging to different ideological backgrounds have unleashed a reign of terror on ordinary citizens, as well as security personnel and officials. The federal interior minister has indicated there is an alliance between Balochistan-based terrorist groups and the TTP. IS-K’s role in this equation is difficult to determine, as in the past the terrorist group has not enjoyed good relations with the BLA. Have these violent groups decided to bury the hatchet and work together against the state? Better intelligence must break any nexus, while the possible resurgence of other terrorist organisations should alert the state to take preventive action. After the Mangi Dam attack, the nation’s top civil and military leadership — including the prime minister and chief of defence forces — met in Quetta and, along with the provincial leadership, vowed to end the wave of terrorism. Yet as the events of the past few weeks have shown, the terrorists continue to wreak havoc. A new strategy is required to bring peace to Balochistan. The CDF on Thursday vowed to restore peace to the troubled province. However, bloodshed in the province has been ongoing — with varying levels of violence — for over two decades, and peace remains elusive. The immediate need is to neutralise terrorist groups of all persuasions so that they are unable to threaten the state or citizens. Hostile foreign actors who may be providing terrorists succour also need to be exposed. In addition to a kinetic response, a complementary political effort is essential. This needs buy-in from the province’s genuine political representatives and all groups that renounce violence. Together with counterterrorism efforts, Balochistan needs compassion and dialogue to restore trust between the state and its people. Published in Dawn, July 25th, 2026

items.title: Tanger : l’exposition « Ne tenir qu’à un fil » de Mohamed Lekleti jusqu’au 30 novembre
items.description: Le Musée de la Kasbah – Espace d’art contemporain à Tanger accueille jusqu’au 30 novembre 2026 l’exposition monographique « Ne tenir qu’à un fil », consacrée au plasticien marocain Mohamed Lekleti, figure reconnue du dessin contemporain en France et au Maroc. Ouverte le 19 juin, l’exposition est organisée dans le cadre de la Saison Méditerranée 2026, portée par l’Institut français, à l’initiative de la Fondation Nationale des Musées du Maroc, en collaboration avec le Frac Occitanie Montpellier. Elle est placée sous le commissariat d’Abdelaziz El Idrissi. À travers cette exposition, le public est invité à pénétrer dans un univers où dessin, peinture, objets et installations se croisent pour interroger les rapports de pouvoir, les mécanismes de domination, l’exil, l’identité et les fragilités de la condition humaine. Le travail de Mohamed Lekleti se distingue d’abord par la place centrale accordée au dessin, mais sa pratique dépasse largement ce seul médium. L’artiste investit également la peinture, le collage, le textile, la sculpture, l’installation et différents objets chargés d’une forte dimension symbolique. Son vocabulaire visuel est particulièrement riche : mains, fils, nuages sombres, corps hybrides mêlant figures humaines et animales, visages dédoublés, silhouettes en tension ou en déséquilibre, enfants, jeux, migrants, hommes de pouvoir, images de guerre, chiffres, formules mathématiques ou encore machines énigmatiques peuplent ses compositions. Des objets inattendus apparaissent également dans son travail, comme des oiseaux naturalisés faisant référence au Cantique des oiseaux de Farîd-ud-Dîn Attâr, des titres de propriété ancestraux marocains gravés dans le bois, des perruques, des masques africains ou encore des tapis de prière. Cette accumulation de signes compose un langage artistique dans lequel les œuvres ne livrent pas immédiatement toutes leurs clés. Chez Mohamed Lekleti, les images invitent davantage à l’interprétation qu’à une lecture unique. « Qui manipule qui ? » Le titre même de l’exposition, « Ne tenir qu’à un fil », renvoie à cette impression de fragilité et d’instabilité qui traverse l’œuvre du plasticien. Dans ses compositions, les personnages et les objets semblent souvent suspendus, comme privés de pesanteur. Hommes, femmes, animaux et machines évoluent dans des espaces où les repères habituels disparaissent et où le monde terrestre semble se confondre avec un univers plus onirique. Le fil constitue à ce titre un motif particulièrement significatif. L’homme apparaît parfois tenant un fil relié à une machine dont la fonction reste indéterminée, elle-même manipulée par des mains dépourvues de corps. Cette question traverse une grande partie de l’exposition. Derrière des compositions qui prennent parfois l’apparence de rébus visuels, Mohamed Lekleti explore les mécanismes de contrôle et d’influence qui structurent les sociétés contemporaines. Les microphones, autre motif récurrent de son œuvre, peuvent ainsi être lus comme des métaphores du discours médiatique, de son pouvoir et de ses possibles illusions. La Méditerranée, l’exil et le déracinement La Méditerranée occupe également une place importante dans l’univers présenté à Tanger. Sa représentation cartographique apparaît dans plusieurs œuvres avec une dimension nécessairement géopolitique. Cette présence renvoie notamment aux migrations, à l’exil et au déracinement. Les tensions perceptibles dans certaines compositions peuvent évoquer l’expérience de celles et ceux contraints de quitter leur terre et de construire leur existence entre plusieurs territoires, cultures ou langues. Cette question du déplacement est étroitement liée au parcours et aux préoccupations artistiques de Mohamed Lekleti. Né à Taza, au Maroc, et vivant et travaillant à Montpellier, en France, l’artiste développe depuis plusieurs années une œuvre nourrie par les questions de mémoire, d’identité et de circulation. Son travail puise aussi dans les mythologies, les récits collectifs et les traditions orales, notamment Les Mille et Une Nuits. Ces références se mêlent à des images contemporaines pour former un univers fragmenté où passé et présent, réalité et imaginaire semblent constamment dialoguer. Une figure du dessin contemporain Lauréat du Salon du dessin contemporain Chic Dessin Paris en 2011, Mohamed Lekleti a progressivement acquis une reconnaissance sur les scènes artistiques française, marocaine et internationale. Son travail a été présenté dans de nombreuses institutions, notamment au Musée d’art contemporain de Lyon, à l’Institut du monde arabe à Paris, au Frissiras Museum, au musée Paul Valéry de Sète, au Musée d’art contemporain de Lisbonne ou encore au Musée Mohammed VI d’art moderne et contemporain à Rabat. L’artiste a également participé à plusieurs rendez-vous internationaux, parmi lesquels Art Dubai, Abu Dhabi Art Fair, 1-54, Art Paris, Volta Basel et Drawing Now. Ses œuvres ont intégré de nombreuses collections publiques et privées à travers le monde, notamment celles du Detroit Institute of Arts, de l’Institut du monde arabe, du MAC Lyon, du Centre national des arts plastiques, du Frac Occitanie, du Musée Mohammed VI, de Bank Al-Maghrib, de la Fondation Blachère ou encore du MACAAL. Une exposition également prévue à Montpellier La Saison Méditerranée 2026 donnera par ailleurs une autre visibilité au travail de Mohamed Lekleti en France. Ses œuvres seront présentées au Frac Occitanie Montpellier dans le cadre de l’exposition « En déséquilibre », sous le commissariat d’Éric Mangion. Son ouverture est annoncée pour le 24 novembre 2026, avant une clôture prévue le 23 décembre. À Tanger, le public dispose encore de plusieurs mois pour découvrir « Ne tenir qu’à un fil », visible jusqu’au 30 novembre 2026 au Musée de la Kasbah – Espace d’art contemporain. Plus qu’une rétrospective linéaire, l’exposition propose une immersion dans le langage singulier de Mohamed Lekleti : un monde peuplé de corps suspendus, de fils, de machines, de symboles et de figures hybrides où les rapports de domination, la mémoire, l’exil et les incertitudes contemporaines se donnent à voir sans jamais imposer une seule interprétation. The post Tanger : l’exposition « Ne tenir qu’à un fil » de Mohamed Lekleti jusqu’au 30 novembre appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Iran calls for expanding strategic cooperation with Pakistan
items.description: ISLAMABAD: As efforts continue to prevent the conflict in the Gulf from widening, Iran on Friday called for expanding strategic cooperation with Pakistan, describing Islamabad’s diplomatic engagement as an important contribution to regional peace and stability. “Pakistan has played a constructive diplomatic role in facilitating negotiations and advancing efforts towards regional peace and stability,” Iran’s Ambassador to Pakistan Reza Amiri Moghadam said while delivering the keynote address at a roundtable discussion, organised by the Centre for International Strategic Studies. “Strengthening our bilateral cooperation is essential for addressing contemporary security challenges in West Asia,” he said. The discussion, titled Pakistan-Iran Relations and Strategic Stab­i­lity in West Asia, brought together diplomats, academics, defence analysts and researchers to examine the future trajectory of Pakistan-Iran relations against the backdrop of an increasingly volatile regional security environment. Opening the discussion, CISS Exec­utive Director Amb Ali Sarwar Naqvi said the recent escalation had generated fresh uncertainties for regional peace, maritime security and global energy markets, making sustained dialogue and regional engagement more important than ever. Former ambassador Masood Khan said Pakistan’s consistent advocacy of peaceful dispute resolution and its ability to maintain constructive relations with regional and international stakeholders had strengthened its credibility as a facilitator of dialogue, confidence-building measures and de-escalation. Director General of the Institute of Strategic Studies, Islamabad, Amb Moinul Haque said the resilience and national unity displayed by the Iranian people during the recent conflict had played an important role in enabling the country to confront the challenges arising from the crisis. Dr Nazish Mahmood of Quaid-i-Azam University said greater cooperation between Pakistan and Iran in border security, trade, energy and regional connectivity could contribute meaningfully to long-term regional stability. Discussing the maritime dimension of the crisis, retired Rear Admiral Faisal Shah highlighted the strategic importance of the Strait of Hormuz as one of the world’s principal energy chokepoints and cautioned that prolonged instability there could carry far-reaching consequences for international trade, energy security and maritime stability. Dr Bilal Zubair, director of research at CISS, said the recent conflict had brought Pakistan and Iran closer than ever before, with their shared border, economic interdependence and common concerns over regional instability reinforcing bilateral cooperation and reshaping the relationship across political, economic and strategic domains. Published in Dawn, July 25th, 2026

items.title: PM again urges Kabul to act against terrorist groups
items.description: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and CDF Field Marshal Asim Munir jointly inaugurate the Sky47 AI Cloud centre.—APP • Says interim Afghan govt has failed to prevent its territory from being used for attacks against Pakistan • Announces Rs300bn Karachi-Chaman dual carriageway, expansion of education, infrastructure and solar projects in Balochistan • Inaugurates Sky47 AI Cloud facility in federal capital ISLAMABAD: Prime Minister Sheh­­baz Sharif on Friday again urg­ed Afghanistan to take action agai­nst terrorist organisations and ensu­­re that Afghan soil was not used for terrorist activities against Pakistan. “Pakistan shares over 2,600-kilometre border with its neighbour and has repeatedly urged the Afghan authorities to act against terrorist organisations and prevent Afghan territory from being used against Pakistan. However, the Afghan interim government has failed to take effective action against these groups,” the prime minister said while addressing the National Workshop on Balochistan. The prime minister reaffirmed the federal government’s commitment to providing all possible resources for the development and prosperity of Balochistan, saying Pakistan could only progress when all provinces advanced equally. He announced that the Rs300 billion dual carriageway project from Karachi to Chaman would be completed within two years. Punjab, he said, had contributed Rs150bn to Balochistan under the National Finance Commission (NFC) Award. He added that other provinces had to play their full role in supporting the Balochistan’s development. The premier said Balochistan had been granted an additional 10 per cent quota in the distribution of laptops and scholarships, and that the Kachhi Canal Project would be completed on a fast-track basis. He praised Balochistan’s contributions to Pakistan’s development and prosperity, saying its leadership had always placed the national interest above personal or political considerations and had wholeheartedly supported the federation. He noted that farmers in Baloch­istan had suffered prolonged power outages for years. To address this issue, around 27,000 agricultural tube wells were being converted to solar energy under a Rs75bn project, to which the federal government had contributed Rs50bn. He expressed deep sorrow over the martyrdom of Mastung Judge Abdul Hakeem Kakar and a security official, praying for the elevation of their ranks and for patience for their families. The prime minister alleged that India was financing terrorism inside Pakistan. He added that although terrorism had largely been eliminated by 2017-18, it later resurfaced through what he described as a highly organised conspiracy. AI cloud centre inaugurated Later, PM Shehbaz described the newly inaugurated AI and cloud computing facility as a landmark achievement for Pakistan, reflecting the country’s growing technological capabilities. Addressing the inauguration ceremony of the country’s first-ever Sky47 AI Cloud centre, the prime minister praised the engineers, experts and institutions involved in the project and said the successful execution of the facility showcased the extraordinary talent available in both Pakistan’s military and civilian sectors. Paying tribute to Chief of Army Staff and Chief of Defence Forces Field Marshal Asim Munir’s leadership, he said the project stood as a testament to what could be achieved when state institutions worked together with a shared national purpose. The prime minister also acknowledged the contributions of Field Marshal Munir, the Ministry of Information Technology, the IT secretary and strategic technology partner ZTE for their roles in delivering the project. The inauguration ceremony was attended by Field Marshal Munir, federal ministers Shaza Fatima Khawaja and Attaullah Tarar, as well as senior government officials. Published in Dawn, July 25th, 2026

items.title: Senators question devolved ministries’ ‘revival’
items.description: • Senate committee says federal role in devolved subjects defies 18th Amendment; forms panel to examine violations • Cabinet division told to scrap proposed IT-related ministries ISLAMABAD: The Senate Standing Committee on Devolution has expressed serious concerns over the re-establishment of federal ministries on subjects already devolved to the provinces under 18th Amend­ment and formed a subcommittee to examine the violations. The requisitioned meeting of the committee was held under the chairmanship of Senator Zamir Hussain Ghumro at Parliament House on Friday. “The continuation of federal ministries on devolved subjects not only contradicts the constitutional scheme but also imposes an unnecessary financial burden on the federal government at a time when austerity measures are being implemented,” Mr Ghumro said. Mr Ghumro said the first notification devolving ministries was issued on Dec 2, 2010, followed by notifications on April 15, 2011, and June 29, 2011, under which 17 ministries on concurrent and provincial subjects were transferred to the provinces. He added that the re-creation of ministries after June 30, 2011, dealing with devolved subjects, amounted to a violation of the Constitution. He cited education, health, national food security, culture, climate change, social initiatives, housing, EOBI, evacuee trust and the collection of Zakat and Ushr among the subjects that had been devolved but where federal ministries or divisions continued to function. The federal structure has expanded to 31 ministries whereas the Constitution envisaged only nine federal ministries — defence, foreign affairs, finance, commerce, communications, maritime affairs, science and technology, law and justice and parliamentary affairs, the senator noted. He said federal expenditure had risen to Rs19 trillion against total tax and non-tax revenue of Rs20tr. “Only defence expenditure can be justified given the war-like conditions,” he said, adding that capping the budget at Rs13tr could save up to Rs6tr. The newly constituted subcommittee will examine violations of the 2010 and 2011 notifications. Additionally, the committee directed the cabinet division to cancel the creation of ministries on IT matters. Senator Poonjo Bheel said these ministries should be abolished, while Senator Jan Muhammad Buledi stressed the need to review the functioning of the Council of Common Interests (CCI), which he said had been made dysfunctional. The Senate panel directed the establishment division to refrain from appointments in devolved subjects, seeking a compliance report within 15 days. It also sought details of payments made to provinces from oil and gas revenues over the last 16 years. Also, the committee was info­rmed that last year Rs46bn allocated for Quaid-i-Azam’s mausoleum were diverted to education ministry. It recommended mont­hly progress reports on the site. The establishment division was directed to provide a complete list of federal secretaries detailing their tenures. Published in Dawn, July 25th, 2026

items.title: Pakistanis captured by Somali pirates victims of ‘ownership crisis’
items.description: “I am the captain of the MT Honour 25, requesting immediate assistance for our vessel. Our condition is extremely critical. Several members of my crew have fallen seriously ill, suffering from diabetes and infections. They are no longer able to hold on,” said Indonesian Captain Ashari Samadikun through a recorded video message dated June 16, 2026. “We are surviving solely on plain white rice and contaminated water. The company has not sent any form of assistance to us. The hijackers refuse to negotiate with any third parties; they only want to negotiate directly with the company listed on our ship’s documents.” The Honour 25 — a Palau-flagged oil tanker carrying 17 to 19 crew members, including 10 Pakistanis — was hijacked by armed pirates off the coast of Puntland, Somalia on April 21, 2026. Three months have gone by and there has been no progress either in negotiations or the payment of the ransom, said to be around $3 million, for the recovery of the hostages. Since its hijack, the crew has made several emotional videos and audio appeals, while reporting that they have run out of clean water, food and medicine. “We are pleading with the government to intervene and compel our company to take responsibility for its crew. We are facing immense difficulties just to stay alive, and to this day, we have seen no progress. The company has provided absolutely zero assistance in terms of food or medicine. We humbly ask for the prayers of all the Indonesian people,” the captain’s message said. As is widely known by now, the ship — besides seven Indonesians — also has 10 Pakistani crew members, as well as an Indian and a Sri Lankan. “We don’t even have clean water to drink; we only have yellowish water to drink from our ship’s tank. We are given plain boiled rice to eat once every 24 hours,” said Pakistani crew member, Oiler Yasir Khan, through a recorded video message dated June 1, 2026. Khan appeals to Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Asim Munir, President Asif Zardari, and “any other relevant authorities” to “please help us or we won’t be able to survive here”. “We only have our government to look up to. Therefore, we ask you to please do something for us so we can go back home and reunite with our families,” he said in the message. These video messages are some of the last communications from the hostages. Yasir Khan, crew member of an oil tanker hijacked by Somali pirates in April, speaks in a video recorded on June 1. — screengrab from video via Shazia Hasan Question of ownership The agency responsible for hiring them, as known to the Pakistani crew, is called Purser Shipping Consultancy (SMC Pvt Limited / Helmsman Shipping Company, North Nazimabad, Karachi). From there, they know an ‘Osman’, but it was revealed later that he may only be a middleman who hired them. In another video message — this time in English — Captain Ashari Samadikun has a book in his hands, showing the name of the ship’s official owners: Wharf Chartering Co of Dubai, who are not interested in talking to the pirates. “This book mentions the ship owner company. There is no mention of anyone named Osman. He must be a middleman only,” he pointed out. Earlier, under the supervision of the Somali pirates, there were several videos and phone calls to the families of the hostages to pressure them to pay the ransom. But after mid-June, the messages stopped. “They used to give us around five or so minutes to speak, but that has all stopped now. The pirates have blocked our WhatsApp,” Ayesha Kashif, wife of Second Officer Syed Kashif Umer Naqvi, told Dawn . “It seems that no one cares, because nothing has changed as far as the government’s stance goes in the recovery of our people. We are only told to be patient. And not having had any communication with our loved ones, think of our state of mind.” “Izhar, my eldest son, failed to appear for his final A-Level exams in May-June. My three younger children also keep enquiring about their father. I’m using our savings to run the house,” she added. Ali Akbar, the older brother of one of the ship’s oilers, Imran Ali, said that both his mother and his sister-in-law — Imran’s wife — have fallen ill with worry. “We are trying to stay strong, but everyone cannot be strong. Our mother is also old,” he said. Oiler Imran Ali, crew member of an oil tanker hijacked by Somali pirates in April. — via Shazia Hasan Mahwish Yasir, the wife of Yasir Khan, said that her husband only tells her about their problems before the phone is taken from him. “The last time that I spoke to him was around Eidul Azha. He told me then that some other pirates also tried taking control of their ship a few days ago, but were told to go away by the pirates already on the ship. It is a crazy situation,” she said. Obaidullah, the older brother of another oiler named Rafiullah Khan, also said that the pirates are no longer interested in talking to them. “They are in touch with the family of only one Pakistani crew member, the ship’s fitter Ameen Bin Shams,” he said. When asked if it was even more worrisome that something might have happened to their relatives, the brother said that anything was possible given the way things were. However, he added that he had a cousin who was also taken hostage by Somali pirates in 2012 and who told him that cutting off contact was a Somali tactic to increase panic. Aisha Ameen, who is now the only person the pirates contact, said that she had also not received any communication for many days. “I keep my cell phone close to me all the time. When they call, they only say to us what they want conveyed, they ignore our queries,” she said. “From what we understood initially … the owner of the ship was Osman. But a WhatsApp message from the pirates to humanitarian Ansar Burney, who also tried to help in resolving the matter, says that ‘Osman’ is a third party in Somalia,” she shared, adding that he was “spreading lies” that the ransom demand was for $10m rather than $3m. Ansar Burney — a former human rights minister — is the chairman of the Ansar Burney Trust, a non-profit human rights organisation working in all areas of human and civil rights worldwide. He has previously participated in efforts to free Pakistanis captured by Somali pirates. “And here we don’t even have any answers from our own government… For instance, the government will not speak to the pirates directly. The ship owner should do that. But it is not established who owns the ship. It is also said that the oil in the ship has a different owner in Yemen,” Ameen told Dawn . “We are only told to remain calm and be patient. But for how long? It has been over three months now.” “By now, there is the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the Ministry of Maritime Affairs, the Pakistan Embassy in Djibouti, this ‘Osman’ fellow claiming to be the ship’s owner, and Ansar Burney pushing them to take action. But we still have no answers, no results,” she added. Crew members of an oil tanker hijacked by Somali pirates in April. — via Shazia Hasan Ameen shared that she has a seven-month-old son whom his father has not seen since he was born, and at her husband’s request, was holding off on the boy’s aqiqah — the sacrificing of an animal upon a child’s birth — until his return. “My three-year-old daughter tells me that she is mad at her father because he no longer talks to her on the phone,” she said. What do I tell her? We are told to stay calm and trust the government. How do I stay calm? Whom do I trust?” Foreign ministry spokesperson Tahir Andrabi said that the government’s efforts to bring the men home continue, adding, “We understand the families’ pain.” The vice chairperson of the Ansar Burney Trust, Shaheen Burney, told Dawn that there had been silence within the government for a long time. However, after the trust kept pushing for action, the matter was referred to the Ministry of Human Rights on the prime minister’s directive. “We went to Islamabad for a detailed meeting regarding the matter with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. They told us that the Pakistan Embassy in Djibouti is also involved,” said Burney. After this, the ministry also held a meeting with the families in Karachi. However, she said, the “same kind of things” were repeated in the meeting, with the ministry reiterating their limitations and that they could “only take the diplomatic way”. After this, she said, PM Shehbaz directed the Ministry of Human Rights to take up the matter. The trust aired its concerns again in a meeting in Islamabad on July 3. Another meeting took place on Friday (July 24), but Ameen has not yet seen the minutes of this one. The Ansar Burney Trust has spoken, in the meantime, to both the ship’s captain — who was worried about the health of his crew — and the pirates, who Burney said do not recognise ‘Osman’ as the ship owner despite his claims, even though he is willing to negotiate. “Almost 100 days have passed since the hijacking and there have been no concrete steps taken by the government in this matter,” she regretted.

items.title: Maritimo target Ghanaian winger Nana Kofi Donkor after impressive season in Georgia
items.description: Portuguese club Marítimo have expressed a strong interest in signing Ghanaian youngster Nana Kofi Donkor following his impressive breakthrough campaign in the Georgian top flight. The 19-year-old winger has emerged as one of the league’s most exciting young talents after joining from Ghana in July 2025 before spending the season on loan at Dinamo Tbilisi. Donkor’s fearless attacking style and ability to beat defenders have made him one of the standout young players in Georgia. The right-footed winger, who predominantly operates from the left flank, has developed one of the most aggressive on-ball profiles in the league, consistently taking on defenders and creating opportunities in the final third. His performances have attracted the attention of Marítimo, who are closely monitoring the teenager as they look to strengthen their squad ahead of the new season. The Portuguese side are understood to be impressed by Donkor’s rapid development, with the winger establishing himself as a key figure during his loan spell at Dinamo Tbilisi. A move to Portugal would represent another significant step in the youngster’s career and provide him with the opportunity to continue his development in one of Europe’s renowned talent-producing leagues. Donkor’s rise is yet another example of Ghana’s growing production line of young players making an impact across Europe, with the teenager now attracting interest after an impressive first full season in professional football.

items.title: Petrol price up by Rs3.66, HSD by Rs4.80 as govt revises fuel rates
items.description: Pakistan fuel prices, 2026 Official ex-depot prices (PKR/litre) — OGRA & Ministry of Energy notifications Petrol (MS-92) Diesel (HSD) Pre-crisis baseline Source: OGRA / Ministry of Energy (Petroleum Division); Dawn.com · "> The government on Friday increased the prices of petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs3.66 and Rs4.80 per litre, respectively, passing on the impact of fluctuating global oil prices following renewed hostilities in the Persian Gulf. Following the changes, the price of petrol stands at Rs335.18 per litre, while that of HSD stands at Rs383.46 per litre. The government is charging a total of Rs110 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs96 on diesel. The Petroleum Division’s notification said the new prices would be applicable for July 25 (Saturday). The diesel price has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28. The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March. Earlier, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US. The government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel. The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends. The daily pricing decision was rejected by the All Pakistan Dealers Association, which said it would consider a protest plan this week. Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes. Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators. Petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

items.title: Sharifs’ pre-poll promises to AJK don’t sit well with PPP
items.description: • Nawaz, Maryam make development pledges, ‘gift’ of 10 electric buses prompts rigging allegations • In apparent swipe at Bilawal, PML-N supremo says ‘Kashmir should not be mistaken for Kashmore, nor Mirpur for Mirpurkhas’ • PPP assails Nawaz’s remarks, urges Election Commission to take notice of ‘promises’ MUZAFFARABAD: PML-N supremo Nawaz Sharif on Friday promised an international airport for Mirpur, the revival of Mansehra-Muzaffarabad-Mirpur mot­o­rway project, and a series of ‘gifts’ for Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK), as he and Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz made a final campaign push for party’s candidates hours before the electioneering ended for the Mirpur division polls. But the pre-poll promises, and an apparent jibe at PPP chief Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari, was not received well by the PML-N’s coalition partner, whose leaders hit back at the elder Sharif, terming his remarks ‘frivolous’ and ‘ridiculous’. Addressing a large public meeting in the lakeside city of Mirpur, the father-daughter duo repeatedly highlighted their Kashmiri roots and told supporters that AJK needed the same infrastructure and welfare-focused governance that had been introduced in Punjab. Describing Kashmir as his “first home”, Mr Sharif said he shared a deep emotional bond with the region. In an apparent swipe at the PPP chairman, Mr Sharif said Kashmir should not be mistaken for Kashmore, nor Mirpur for Mirpurkhas. Mentioning Mr Bhutto-Zardari by name for the first time during his election campaign in AJK, he said: “Don’t take this the wrong way, Bilawal bhai . You are like a son to me.” “Political sparring among parties should continue. There can even be some sharp exchanges, and that’s perfectly healthy. But there should be no fighting or violence.” “We have come with a pledge that, God willing, we will change the destiny of Mirpur and all of Azad Kashmir,” he said, while asking successive governments in Pakistan and AJK what they had done for the region since his ouster. He said the PML-N’s manifesto accorded priority to education and healthcare, promising new schools, colleges and universities as well as hospitals equipped with CT scanners and MRI facilities so that residents would not have to travel to Pakistan for treatment. Nawaz also announced a gift of 10 ‘Hospitals on Wheels’ and as many electric green buses for Mirpur from the Punjab government. He also pledged to dualise the Kotli-Nakyal road, construct tunnels at Lohar Gali and Leepa Valley in Muzaffarabad division, re­­v­­ive the long-stalled motorway project linking Mans­ehra, Muzaffarabad and Mirpur along the Jhelum River, and seek the establishment of an international airport in Mirpur. Speaking after him, CM Maryam argued that AJK did not suffer from a lack of resources but from inadequate infrastructure, insu­fficient welfare program­mes and poor governance. She asked the audience who had built the Kohala-Muzaffarabad Road, the Murree-Kohala Road and cardiac hospitals, prompting chants of “Nawaz Sharif” from the crowd. The Punjab CM pledged that welfare schemes introduced by the PML-N government in Punjab would be extended to AJK immediately after the elections, saying voters should support the party if they wanted development. “The world will see a clean Azad Kashmir after the elections,” she said, urging people to “think carefully” before casting their ballots. PPP hits back The announcement of schemes for AJK, including the ‘gift’ of 10 e-buses, during the campaign did not go well with the PPP. PPP-Parliamentarians Secretary General Nayyar Bukhari strongly criticised the PML-N leadership for gifting 10 electric buses, bearing CM Maryam’s images, to AJK during the election campaign and described the move as “political bribery”. He demanded the chief election commissioner take immediate notice of the transfer of the buses. Some PPP candidates for AJK Assembly elections, including Sardar Javed Ayub, Sardar Mukhtar Abbasi and Syed Bazil Ali Naqvi, also opposed the PML-N move. Taking exception to Mr Sharif’s remarks about the PPP chief, AJK Legislative Assembly Spe­aker and PPP candidate Chaudhry Latif Akbar alleged a series of promises made by PML-N leaders during their election rallies constituted a violation of the election code of conduct, and called on the Election Commission to take strict notice. He told the presser the announcements amounted to an attempt to woo voters ahead of polls. Taking exception to Mr Sharif’s light-hearted remark at a Muzaffarabad rally that he would ask Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif to make the PML-N’s nominee the next prime minister of AJK, Mr Akbar quipped: “Nawaz Sharif’s own brother did not make him prime minister, yet he comes here and complains about it.” Referring to Punjab CM Maryam Nawaz’s claims, Mr Akbar alleged the PML-N leadership was attempting to “buy Kashmiri votes” through pre-election promises. Separately, Sindh Information Minister Sharjeel Inam Memon hit back at Mr Sharif’s jibe, saying: “Do not make the land and people of Sindh and Kashmir a subject of ridicule and humour”. Political differences ha­­ve their place, but ridicule of any province, city or area is not acceptable un­­­der any circumstances, he said, terming the ex-PM’s remarks “not only frivolous but also ridiculous”. Published in Dawn, July 25th, 2026

items.title: Another bid to mend US-Iran fences ‘with China’s blessing’
items.description: TEHRAN: Iranian-made ‘Zulfiqar’ missiles are displayed at Azadi Square. As the US kept up its missile strikes on Iranian targets, the IRGC vowed to ‘kill a member of the US forces for every Iranian killed’.—AFP • Exploratory talks held during Iranian interior minister’s recent Islamabad visit • Dar meets Araghchi at SCO summit; Qatar calls for implementing Islamabad MoU • Beijing concerned as Red Sea closure would compound Hormuz woes • Trump says Iran getting serious about talks; warns China, Russia against ‘getting involved’ in conflict • Says US will punish Iran for attacks on ships by Houthi rebels • Four die as US continues strikes on Iran ISLAMABAD / DUBAI: Pakistan is said to be exploring a path towards a resumption of stalled US-Iran talks to end their nearly five-month-old war, following a push initiated by China. The development came as US missiles struck targets across Iran on Friday after President Donald Trump vowed “major military punishment” for Tehran and its Houthi allies in Yemen for extending the Middle East war to a second major shipping chokepoint, the mouth of the Red Sea. According to Reuters , exploratory discussions for the fresh push towards talks took place during a visit by Iran’s Interior Minister Eskandar Momeni to Islamabad this week , his second within the last 10 days. Earlier this week, Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthi rebels had declared a naval blockade against Saudi Arabia , which signed a mutual defence treaty with Pakistan last year. Beijing, which has consistently backed Pakistan’s mediation efforts, had dispatched its special envoy in March to lead a shuttle-diplomacy trip around the Middle East. China’s interests are being harmed by the closure of the Strait of Hormuz, and disruptions to the Red Sea route would hit another key trade route Beijing relies on. In a statement, China’s foreign ministry said “China supports the mediation efforts made by Pakistan and other parties.” It added that China will continue to “play an active role in restoring peace and tranquility in the Middle East Gulf region as soon as possible.” Separately, Qatar’s Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al Thani called on all parties to commit to dialogue and to implement the terms of the memorandum of understanding between the United States and Iran. This includes “ensuring freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz, to preserve regional security, safeguard the gains achieved, and enhance regional stability”, the Qatari foreign ministry said. Sheikh Mohammed made the remarks in Doha during a meeting with the new British foreign secretary, Ed Miliband. Implementing the memorandum was necessary to preserve regional security, safeguard the gains achieved and strengthen stability, Sheikh Mohammed said, reiterating Qatar’s full support for efforts to defuse tensions and reach a comprehensive agreement securing lasting peace in the region. ‘Serious about talks’ Meanwhile, US President Donald Trump said Friday that he had not decided on whether to launch major strikes on Iran as Tehran was now getting “very serious” in talks with Washington. “Look, we’re talking to them right now. I think they’re getting more and more serious as the days go by, for maybe the obvious reason.” Earlier, in a Truth Social post on Friday, Trump said that he does not believe China or Russia are “participating” in the ongoing Iran conflict, but warned that if they did get inv­o­lved “it would be very bad for them”. Trump also said that he would hold Iran accountable for any further attacks by Yemeni fighters, “and major military punishment will be inflicted upon Iran and, of course, the Houthis, themselves”. Iranian media cited the head of Iran’s top joint military command as saying Iran would kill a member of the US forces for every Iranian killed. On Friday, US missiles struck a Revolutionary Guards Navy headquarters in the Ziba Kenar area of the Caspian Sea province of Gilan, according to a security official in Gilan. Provincial authorities said US projectiles had also struck the port city of Bandar Anzali, according to the ILNA news agency. Four people were killed and five injured in a US attack on the Iranian city of Ahvaz, the state broadcaster IRIB said. Diplomatic contacts Meanwhile, Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar held a meeting with his Iranian counterpart, Abbas Ara­g­hchi, on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation’s Council of Foreign Ministers Meeting in Cholpon-Ata, Kyrgyzstan. In a statement, the Foreign Office said the two top diplomats reviewed the ongoing regional situation and bilateral ties. “DPM/FM expressed deep concern over recent regional tensions and underscored the importance of dialogue, restraint, de-escalation by all sides, and sustained diplomatic engagement to achieve lasting peace and stability,” the FO said in a post on X. “He emphasised the need to build on the understandings reached und­er the Islamabad MoU of June 2026.” “The two sides agreed to maintain close coordination and regular consultations on issues of mutual interest and reaffirmed their commitment to working together for regional peace, stability and shared prosperity,” the statement concluded. Separately, in his remarks at the SCO summit, Mr Dar said: “Pakistan firmly believes that dialogue, diplomacy and mutual respect provide the only sustainable way forward to resolve conflicts and achieve durable peace and security.” He added that this principle led to Pakistan hosting talks between the United States and Iran in Islamabad in April, “enabling first high-level direct diplomatic contact between the two sides after 47 years”. Mr Dar then urged the international community to seize the opportunity provided by the Islamabad MoU and US-Iran technical talks to push for lasting peace. Published in Dawn, July 25th, 2026

Chinese FM meets Tajik counterpart
items.description: Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi met with Tajik Foreign Minister Sirojiddin Muhriddin on Friday on the sidelines of the Meeting of the Council of the Ministers of Foreign Affairs of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) Member States in Kyrgyzstan. Wang, also a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, said that in May this year, Tajik President Emomali Rahmon paid a successful state visit to China. The most important outcome of the visit was the signing of the China-Tajikistan Treaty on Permanent Good-Neighborliness, Friendship and Cooperation, which set a precedent in Central Asia, Wang said. The two sides also issued the Joint Statement between the People's Republic of China and the Republic of Tajikistan on Deepening the Comprehensive Strategic Cooperative Partnership in the New Era, demonstrating their determination to jointly promote the building of a China-Tajikistan community with a shared future, Wang said. The common task of the foreign ministries of the two countries is to translate the consensus reached by the two heads of state into concrete actions, make plans for exchanges at various levels, and promote deeper and more substantive cooperation in areas including energy, connectivity and counterterrorism and security, so as to deliver more cooperation outcomes benefiting the people of both countries, Wang said. Muhriddin said Rahmon's visit to China this year was a great success and yielded fruitful results, further consolidating high-level mutual trust, and opening a new chapter in bilateral relations. China has become Tajikistan's largest trade and economic partner, he said, adding that Tajikistan is confident in the prospects of bilateral cooperation. Tajikistan is willing to work with China to fully implement the consensuses reached during Rahmon's visit, strengthen practical cooperation in areas including energy, jointly combat terrorism, and elevate the Tajikistan-China comprehensive strategic cooperative partnership in the new era to a higher level, Muhriddin said.

items.title: SpaceX's Starship rocket lifts off from Texas for 13th test flight
items.description: SpaceX's Starship rocket lifted off from Texas on Friday and deployed its first 20 upgraded Starlink satellites into suborbital ​space, one of many testing goals in the company's 13th test mission as it ‌races to begin routine service with the rocket by the end of the year. The roughly 122-meter-tall Starship rocket system blasted off around 6:50 p.m. ET (2250 GMT) from SpaceX's Starbase company town, with the Super Heavy first stage booster sending its ​Starship upper stage on a suborbital trajectory. The roughly hour-long mission will conclude with Starship's reentry ​through Earth's atmosphere and a splashdown in the Indian Ocean. As Starship approached 26,400 kilometers per hour in space some 10 minutes into its flight, the Super Heavy booster returned ​to Earth and impacted the Gulf of Mexico harder than expected, SpaceX said, though it had reignited more ​engines than its botched return in May during a previous test flight. The Starship test flight is SpaceX's 13th since 2023, featuring a new version of the rocket crucial to the company's plans to expand Starlink, land humans on the moon for ​NASA and eventually deploy thousands of artificial intelligence-processing satellites in orbit. Twenty minutes into its spaceflight, Starship began ​deploying 20 Starlink V3 satellites, dispensing them one by one via the ship's "Pez"-like payload deployment. Flying over a shadowed Earth, ‌thunderstorms ⁠with flashes of lightning were visible in the background 190 kilometers below, according to a camera fixed to the rocket and streamed live by SpaceX. A crowd of SpaceX engineers in SpaceX's Hawthorne, California, facilities could be heard on the live stream cheering at the rocket's mission milestones, at one point chanting "USA." While in ​space, the Starlink satellites – a ​new "V3" version with ⁠greater bandwidth capabilities – will deploy solar arrays and antennae to briefly connect with SpaceX's Starlink network of some 10,000 satellites orbiting above. The Starlinks are the first to ​be deployed by Starship, though they will follow the ship's suborbital trajectory into ​Earth's atmosphere ⁠and burn up. Some of them have spotlights and cameras that will record Starship's heat shield as it hits intense atmospheric friction later in the mission, giving SpaceX key testing insight into how well the rocket survives its ⁠return from ​space. SpaceX plans to use Starship by the end of 2026 ​to begin launching thousands of Starlink V3 satellites, expanding the constellation's capacity to be able to connect directly to mobile devices such ​as cell phones. The current network only connects to Starlink-branded dishes.

items.title: DEPF : hausse de 0,4% de la production nationale en énergie électrique
items.description: La Direction des études et des prévisions financières (DEPF), a indiqué que la production de l’énergie électrique, au niveau national, a légèrement augmenté de 0,4% au terme des cinq premiers mois de 2026, après une croissance de 5,4% un an plus tôt. Dans sa récente note de conjoncture, la DEPF fait savoir que les échanges de l’énergie électrique avec l’extérieur, le volume importé s’est accru de 43% à fin mai dernier, après une hausse de 8,7% un an auparavant. De son côté, le volume exporté s’est replié de 40,8% (après -20,5%) et ce, dans un contexte d’accroissement de 4,1% du volume d’énergie nette appelée, après une hausse de 5,2% l’année dernière. Pour ce qui est de la consommation d’énergie électrique, elle s’est appréciée de 8,7% à fin mai 2026, après une consolidation de 14,2% un an auparavant. Au cours des deux premiers mois du T2-2026, la production de l’énergie électrique au niveau national s’est améliorée de 2,2%. Cette progression revient à l’augmentation de la production privée (+3,4%) et de celle des énergies renouvelables relatives à la loi 13-09 (+15,8%), conjuguée au dynamisme de l’apport des tiers nationaux (+285,3%). The post DEPF : hausse de 0,4% de la production nationale en énergie électrique appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Chinese FM meets Iranian counterpart, urges resumption of negotiations
items.description: Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi met with his Iranian counterpart Seyed Abbas Araghchi on Friday, calling for an early resumption of negotiations and the implementation of a memorandum of understanding (MoU) aimed at easing tensions in the Middle East and the Gulf region. The meeting took place on the sidelines of the Meeting of the Council of the Ministers of Foreign Affairs of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization Member States in Cholpon-Ata, Kyrgyzstan. Wang, also a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, said China is deeply concerned about the renewed escalation of tensions in the Middle East and the Gulf region. He said the MoU signed more than a month ago was a valuable outcome of mediation efforts by multiple parties and reflected the aspirations of the Iranian people and other peoples in the region for peace and stability. The progress achieved through dialogue should not be abandoned, he added. "The door to negotiations, once opened, should not be closed, and as long as there is hope for peace, it should not be given up," Wang said. He stressed that the immediate priority is to resolve differences through dialogue and negotiations and resume implementation of the consensus reached in the MoU. As a comprehensive strategic partner of Iran, China firmly supports Iran in safeguarding its sovereignty, security and national dignity, Wang said. He added that China will continue to act in line with the four-point proposal on maintaining and promoting peace and stability in the Middle East, support mediation efforts by Pakistan and other parties, facilitate the early resumption of dialogue and negotiations, properly address issues related to the Strait of Hormuz, improve relations among neighboring countries, advance collective security among Gulf states and help restore peace and stability in the Middle East at an early date. Araghchi briefed Wang on the latest developments in the Middle East and the Gulf region, stressing that Iran's willingness to negotiate remains unchanged and Tehran does not wish to see the conflict continue. He urged the United States to honor its commitments, exercise restraint, work with Iran toward the same goal and seek a reasonable solution. Araghchi said it is crucial for Iran and China, as comprehensive strategic partners, to strengthen communication and coordination at the current critical moment. He thanked China for consistently maintaining an objective and impartial position and promoting peace and dialogue, and expressed hope that China would continue to play an important role in helping ease regional tensions.

items.title: Chinese FM Wang Yi meets Pakistani counterpart
items.description: Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi met with Pakistani Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Mohammad Ishaq Dar on Friday on the sidelines of the Meeting of the Council of the Ministers of Foreign Affairs of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) Member States in Kyrgyzstan. Wang, also a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, said China-Pakistan relations have always remained at the forefront of the times. The two sides should jointly implement the important consensus reached by the leaders of the two countries, actively advance exchanges at all levels and cooperation across various fields, and accelerate the building of an even closer China-Pakistan community with a shared future, Wang said. China highly appreciates Pakistan's key role in facilitating the memorandum of understanding reached between the United States and Iran, Wang said, adding that China will continue to firmly support Pakistan in its efforts to mediate, promote the return of all parties to dialogue and negotiations, and achieve a lasting ceasefire. China is ready to strengthen coordination with Pakistan on multilateral platforms such as the SCO and the United Nations to safeguard the common interests of the two countries and the legitimate rights and interests of the Global South, Wang said. Dar said it is essential for Pakistan and China to maintain communication and coordination on all occasions. The sudden escalation of the situation in the Middle East and the Gulf serves the interests of no party, he said, adding that Pakistan is willing to continue its efforts in peace mediation and appreciates China's consistent support and assistance. Pakistan is ready to strengthen coordination with China under multilateral frameworks such as the SCO and the China-Pakistan-Bangladesh trilateral cooperation mechanism, and make due contributions to safeguarding regional peace, stability and development, he said.

items.title: Chinese FM Wang Yi meets Russian counterpart
items.description: Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi met with Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov on Friday on the sidelines of the Meeting of the Council of the Ministers of Foreign Affairs of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) Member States in Kyrgyzstan. Wang, also a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, said that the meeting between the two heads of state in May in Beijing has ushered bilateral relations into a new stage of greater achievements and faster development. China wishes Russia success in its State Duma elections to be held in September and firmly supports the choice independently made by the Russian people, Wang said. Noting that this year marks the 25th anniversary of the signing of the China-Russia Treaty of Good-Neighborliness and Friendly Cooperation and the 25th anniversary of the SCO, Wang said the treaty has guided the two countries in setting an example of a new type of state-to-state and major-country relations. The SCO has become a force for global stability with growing international influence, Wang said, adding that both sides should jointly support the organization's development, carry forward the Shanghai Spirit and inject new vitality into improving global governance and building a community with a shared future for humanity. China and Russia should strengthen strategic coordination, uphold the outcomes of World War II and never allow Japan to rearm, Wang said, adding that he expected Russia to continue supporting the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) "China Year" events, and called for closer coordination and mutual support in multilateral frameworks including the United Nations. Lavrov said head-of-state diplomacy serves as an important driving force for Russia-China relations. President Putin's successful visit to China this year and the more than 50 meetings between the two heads of state have continuously elevated bilateral relations to new heights, he said. He congratulated China on successfully hosting the World Artificial Intelligence (AI) Conference, noting that Russia has joined the World AI Cooperation Organization and looks forward to deepening bilateral cooperation in innovation and science and technology through this platform. Russia remains highly vigilant against and firmly opposes Japan's accelerated remilitarization and pursuit of nuclear weapons capability, he said. The two sides can further strengthen strategic coordination within multilateral frameworks such as the United Nations, APEC, the Group of Twenty, BRICS and East Asia Cooperation, and jointly promote a more democratic and equitable multipolar world, he added. The two sides also had an in-depth exchange of views on international and regional issues of common concern.

items.title: Ghanaian youngster Isaac Assibu signs new Malmo deal, earns first-team promotion
items.description: Ghanaian youngster Isaac Assibu has been rewarded for his impressive development at Swedish champions Malmö FF after signing a long-term contract extension and earning a permanent promotion to the club’s first team. The 18-year-old winger has committed his future to the Allsvenskan giants until 2030 , capping a remarkable rise since joining the club from the West Africa Football Academy (WAFA) in 2025. Assibu initially featured for Malmö’s U19 side, where he quickly established himself as one of the team’s standout performers. Before the mid-season break, he scored three goals in six U19 Allsvenskan appearances, form that convinced the club’s technical staff to accelerate his development. His performances earned him regular training opportunities with the senior side before he was included in the matchday squad for Malmö’s league clash against IFK Göteborg. The teenager later made his Allsvenskan debut as a second-half substitute against Kalmar FF, marking another important milestone in his burgeoning career. Isaac Assibu has earned a contract extension with Malmö FF and has been permanently promoted to the club's first team after impressing on his Allsvenskan debut. The Ghanaian youngster, who joined from West Africa Football Academy, has steadily risen through Malmö's academy… pic.twitter.com/lzD2AFNG4g — Joseph Ayinga-Walter (@AyingaWalter) July 24, 2026 Comfortable on either flank, Assibu has impressed with his explosive pace, close control and ability to beat defenders in one-on-one situations, qualities that have made him one of the club’s brightest young prospects. Malmö sporting director Philip Berglund believes the Ghanaian has earned his promotion through his performances and attitude. “Isaac has shown an X-factor and a mentality in training that we have all been impressed with. It will be exciting to continue to follow Isaac’s development as he is now permanently promoted to our men’s team from P19. We are very happy to sign a contract with him beyond 2030,” Berglund said. Assibu expressed his delight after extending his stay with the Swedish champions. “I am very happy to extend my contract. I feel good in Malmö, it is a nice place and I am getting into it more and more. It has been a very good experience to train with the first team every day and it has made me develop,” he said. The Ghanaian also reflected on his top-flight debut and his ambitions for the future. “It was fantastic to make my debut in the Allsvenskan. I just want to continue developing as a player and in the future I hope I can help the team win more titles.” The contract extension and first-team promotion underline Malmö’s confidence in the teenager’s potential and represent another significant milestone for one of Ghana’s most exciting young talents abroad. Assibu’s rise also continues the growing influence of Ghanaian players in Scandinavian football, with the winger hoping to follow in the footsteps of several compatriots who have used Sweden as a platform to establish themselves at the highest level.
